plans.evaluator_notes:
Premium is per person. For a couple, each spouse needs a plan, so double the annual premium and the out-of-pocket exposure (the app currently doubles individual amounts for a married couple).
Medical deductible is $0, so every service pays its copay or coinsurance from the first dollar.
Several services have a price per site of service (imaging, X-ray, diagnostic tests, surgery). The file holds one site per service; the others are in each service's limits text. Adjust Evaluator prices if you use a different site.
Part D has its own $700 deductible for tiers 4 and 5 and a $2,400 prescription out-of-pocket cap (limits.drug_deductible, limits.drug_oop_max).

Where a price differs by site of service, the file uses: freestanding radiological facility for X-rays ($40) and advanced imaging ($205), specialist's office for diagnostic tests ($20), ambulatory surgery center for surgery ($0; outpatient hospital surgery is $450), and a diabetic supplier for diabetic supplies (20%). Other sites are in each limits text.
service_area lists King County only (the county of the other plan files); the plan also serves Kitsap, Pierce and Snohomish.
Skilled nursing: $221 per day for days 21-100 is entered with max_units 80; the $10 per day for days 1-20 is not modeled.

Dental: the $4,000 yearly maximum covers preventive and comprehensive dental together, so cleanings count toward it. It is treated as per person.

plans.evaluator_notes:
Premium is per person. For a couple, each spouse needs a plan, so double the annual premium and the out-of-pocket exposure (the app currently doubles individual amounts for a married couple).
Medical deductible in-network is $0, so every in-network service pays its copay or coinsurance from the first dollar.
Coinsurance-only items (drug tiers 3-5, DME 20%) have no dollar price on the plan page. Enter your own prices to cost them.
Out-of-network cost shares are recorded in out_of_network_services; the evaluator costs in-network use.
Part D has its own $700 deductible for tiers 3-5 and a $2,400 annual prescription out-of-pocket cap (limits.drug_deductible, limits.drug_oop_max).
